rules.title: KYC Policy Framework
rules.description: NBFCs must formulate and put in place a proper policy framework on 'Know Your Customer' and Anti-Money Laundering measures with the approval of the Board within three months of the date of the circular.
rules.source_clause: All NBFCs are, therefore, advised to adopt the same with suitable modifications depending on the activity undertaken by them and ensure that a proper policy framework on ‘Know Your Customer’ and Anti-Money Laundering measures is formulated and put in place with the approval of the Board within three months of the date of this circular.

rules.title: Compliance with KYC Guidelines
rules.description: NBFCs must ensure full compliance with the KYC guidelines by themselves and persons authorised by them, including brokers/agents, and accept full consequences of any violation.
rules.source_clause: As regards deposits collected by persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc. inasmuch as such persons are collecting the deposits on behalf of the NBFC, it shall be the sole responsibility of the NBFC to ensure full compliance with the KYC guidelines by such persons.

rules.title: Due Diligence of Authorised Persons
rules.description: NBFCs must put in place a process of due diligence in respect of persons authorised by them, including brokers/agents, collecting deposits on their behalf through a uniform policy for appointment and detailed verification.
rules.source_clause: As an extension of the KYC Guidelines, NBFCs should put in place a process of due diligence in respect of persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc. collecting deposits on behalf of the company through a uniform policy for appointment and detailed verification.

rules.title: KYC Guidelines Applicability
rules.description: The instructions contained in the master circular are applicable to all NBFCs, and contravention or non-compliance will attract penalties under the relevant provisions of the Act.
rules.source_clause: The instructions, contained in the master circular, are applicable to all NBFCs. These guidelines are issued under Sections 45K and 45L of the RBI Act, 1934 and any contravention of the same or non-compliance will attract penalties under the relevant provisions of the Act.

rules.title: KYC Procedure Simplification for Low-Income Groups
rules.description: NBFCs may open accounts for persons who intend to keep balances not exceeding Rs. 50,000 and total credit not exceeding Rs. 1,00,000 in a year, subject to introduction from another account holder who has been subjected to full KYC procedure or any other evidence as to the identity and address of the customer to the satisfaction of the NBFC.
rules.source_clause: It was clarified in March 2006 that although flexibility in the requirement of documents of identity and proof of address has been provided in the circular mentioned above yet there may be instances where certain persons, especially, those belonging to low income group both in urban and rural areas may not be able to produce such documents to satisfy the NBFC about their identity and address.

rules.title: Introduction and Verification Requirements
rules.description: The introducer's account with the NBFC should be at least six months old and should show satisfactory transactions. Photograph of the customer who proposes to open the account and also his address needs to be certified by the introducer.
rules.source_clause: a) introduction from another account holder who has been subjected to full KYC procedure. The introducer’s account with the NBFC should be at least six month old and should show satisfactory transactions. Photograph of the customer who proposes to open the account and also his address needs to be certified by the introducer.

rules.title: Notification and Documentation Requirements
rules.description: The customer should be made aware that if at any point of time, the balances in all his/her accounts with the NBFC (taken together) exceeds Rs. 50,000 or total credit in the account exceeds Rs. 1,00,000, no further transactions will be permitted until the full KYC procedure is completed.
rules.source_clause: While opening accounts as described above, the customer should be made aware that if at any point of time, the balances in all his/her accounts with the NBFC (taken together) exceeds rupees fifty thousand (Rs. 50,000/-) or total credit in the account exceeds rupees one lakh (Rs. 1,00,000/-), no further transactions will be permitted until the full KYC procedure is completed.

rules.title: Periodic Review of Risk Categorization
rules.description: NBFCs are required to put in place a system of periodical review of risk categorisation of accounts and the need for applying enhanced due diligence measures in case of higher risk perception on a customer. The review should be carried out at a periodicity of not less than once in six months.
rules.source_clause: NBFCs are required to put in place a system of periodical review of risk categorisation of accounts and the need for applying enhanced due diligence measures in case of higher risk perception on a customer. NBFCs are further advised that such review of risk categorisation of customers should be carried out at a periodicity of not less than once in six months.

rules.title: Updation of Customer Identification Data
rules.description: NBFCs should introduce a system of periodical updation of customer identification data (including photograph/s) after the account is opened. The periodicity of such updation should not be less than once in five years in case of low risk category customers and not less than once in two years in case of high and medium risk categories.
rules.source_clause: NBFCs also introduce a system of periodical updation of customer identification data (including photograph/s) after the account is opened. The periodicity of such updation should not be less than once in five years in case of low risk category customers and not less than once in two years in case of high and medium risk categories.

rules.title: KYC/AML Guidelines for Overseas Branches
rules.description: KYC/AML guidelines issued by Reserve Bank of India shall also apply to their branches and majority owned subsidiaries located outside India, especially, in countries which do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations, to the extent local laws permit.
rules.source_clause: NBFCs have been further advised in terms of extant instructions that KYC/AML guidelines issued by Reserve Bank of India shall also apply to their branches and majority owned subsidiaries located outside India, especially, in countries which do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations, to the extent local laws permit.

rules.title: Acceptance of Aadhaar Letter
rules.description: The letter issued by Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) containing details of name, address and Aadhaar number is recognised as an officially valid document for opening of accounts.
rules.source_clause: The Government of India issued a Notification No. 14/2010/F.No. 6/2/2007-ES dated December 16, 2010 which recognises the letter issued by Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) containing details of name, address and Aadhaar number, as an officially valid document as contained in Rule 2(1)(d) of the PML Rules, 2005.

rules.title: Unique Customer Identification Code (UCIC)
rules.description: NBFCs were advised to initiate steps for allotting Unique Customer Identification Code (UCIC) to all their customers while entering into any new relationships. Existing individual customers may also be allotted UCIC by end-June 2013.
rules.source_clause: Consequently, NBFCs were advised to initiate steps for allotting Unique Customer Identification Code (UCIC) to all their customers while entering into any new relationships. Similarly, existing individual customers may also be allotted UCIC by end-June 2013.

rules.title: Due Diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs)
rules.description: Detailed guidelines on Customer Due Diligence (CDD) measures to be made applicable to Politically Exposed Person (PEP) and their family members or close relatives are contained in Annex VII to the Master Circular No.151/03.10.42/2009-10 dated July 1, 2009.
rules.source_clause: Detailed guidelines on Customer Due Diligence (CDD) measures to be made applicable to Politically Exposed Person (PEP) and their family members or close relatives are contained in Annex VII to the Master Circular No.151/03.10.42/2009-10 dated July 1, 2009.

rules.title: Identification of Beneficial Owners of Professional Intermediaries
rules.description: NBFCs should identify the beneficial owners of client accounts opened by professional intermediaries, and verify their identity in a manner that satisfies the NBFC that it knows who the beneficial owners are.
rules.source_clause: 13. Client accounts opened by professional intermediaries

rules.title: Prohibition on Professional Intermediaries with Confidentiality Obligations
rules.description: NBFCs should not allow professional intermediaries with confidentiality obligations to open or hold accounts on behalf of clients, if they are unable to disclose the true identity of the account owner or beneficial owner.
rules.source_clause: 13. Client accounts opened by professional intermediaries

rules.title: Customer Identification Procedure for Proprietary Concerns
rules.description: NBFCs should frame internal guidelines for customer identification procedure for proprietary concerns, and verify documents such as proof of name, address, and activity of the concern.
rules.source_clause: accounts of proprietary concerns

rules.title: Appointment of Principal Officer
rules.description: NBFCs should appoint a senior management officer as Principal Officer, who should have timely access to customer identification data and other CDD information, and be able to act independently and report directly to senior management or the Board of Directors.
rules.source_clause: 15. Principal Officer

rules.title: Suspicion of Money Laundering/Terrorist Financing
rules.description: NBFCs should carry out full-scale customer due diligence (CDD) before opening an account if there is suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing.
rules.source_clause: 16. Suspicion of money laundering/terrorist financing - With a view to preventing NBFCs  from being used, intentionally or unintentionally, by criminal elements for money laundering or terrorist financing, it was clarified that whenever there is suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing or when other factors give rise to a belief that the customer does not, in fact, pose a low risk, NBFCs were advised to carry out full scale customer due diligence (CDD) before opening an account.

rules.title: Filing of Suspicious Transaction Report (STR)
rules.description: NBFCs should file an STR with FIU-IND if they believe that they would no longer be satisfied that they know the true identity of the account holder.
rules.source_clause: 17. Filing of Suspicious Transaction Report (STR)

rules.title: Maintenance of Records of Transactions
rules.description: NBFCs should maintain proper records of transactions, including cash transactions of more than Rs. 10 lakh, and suspicious transactions.
rules.source_clause: 2. Maintenance of records of transactions

rules.title: Information to be Preserved
rules.description: NBFCs should preserve information on transactions, including nature, amount, date, and parties to the transaction.
rules.source_clause: 3. Information to be preserved

rules.title: Maintenance and Preservation of Records
rules.description: NBFCs should maintain and preserve account information, including records of transactions and customer identification, for at least ten years.
rules.source_clause: 4.   Maintenance and Preservation of records

rules.title: Preservation of Customer Records
rules.description: Records pertaining to the identification of the customer and his address must be preserved for at least ten years after the business relationship is ended.
rules.source_clause: records pertaining to the identification of the customer and his address (e.g. copies of documents like passports, identity cards, driving licenses, PAN card, utility bills etc.) obtained while opening the account and during the course of business relationship, as indicated in paragraph 4 of the of the above said Master Circular dated July 1, 2009, would continue to be preserved for at least ten years after the business relationship is ended as required under Rule 10 of the Rules ibid.

rules.title: Reporting to Financial Intelligence Unit-India
rules.description: NBFCs are required to report information relating to cash and suspicious transactions to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).
rules.source_clause: It is advised that in terms of the PMLA rules, NBFCs are required to report information relating to cash and suspicious transactions to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) at the following address:

rules.title: Cash Transaction Report (CTR) Submission
rules.description: The cash transaction report (CTR) for each month should be submitted to FIU-IND by 15th of the succeeding month.
rules.source_clause: The cash transaction report (CTR) for each month should be submitted to FIU-IND by 15th of the succeeding month.

rules.title: Confidentiality in Reporting
rules.description: Utmost confidentiality should be maintained in filing of CTR and STR with FIU-IND.
rules.source_clause: Utmost confidentiality should be maintained in filing of CTR and STR with FIU-IND.

rules.title: Electronic Filing of Reports
rules.description: NBFCs should initiate urgent steps to ensure electronic filing of cash transaction report (CTR) as early as possible.
rules.source_clause: It would be necessary for NBFCs to initiate urgent steps to ensure electronic filing of cash transaction report (CTR) as early as possible.

rules.title: Customer Profile and Risk Categorization
rules.description: NBFCs are required to prepare a profile for each customer based on risk categorization and review it periodically.
rules.source_clause: In terms of instructions contained in the guidelines on ‘Know Your Customer Norms’ and ‘Anti-Money Laundering Measures’ of our circular dated February 21, 2005, NBFCs are required to prepare a profile for each customer based on risk categorization.

rules.title: Software Application for Transaction Monitoring
rules.description: NBFCs are required to put in place an appropriate software application to throw alerts when the transactions are inconsistent with risk categorization and updated profile of customers.
rules.source_clause: It is needless to add that a robust software throwing alerts is essential for effective identification and reporting of suspicious transactions.

rules.title: Threshold for Cash Transactions
rules.description: The cut-off limit of Rupees ten lakh is applicable to integrally connected cash transactions.
rules.source_clause: In regard to CTR, it is reiterated that the cut-off limit of Rupees ten lakh is applicable to integrally connected cash transactions also.

rules.title: Reporting of Counterfeit Currency Transactions
rules.description: All cash transactions, where forged or counterfeit Indian currency notes have been used as genuine should be reported by the Principal Officer to FIU-IND immediately.
rules.source_clause: All cash transactions, where forged or counterfeit Indian currency notes have been used as genuine should be reported by the Principal Officer to FIU-IND immediately in the format (Counterfeit Currency Report – CCR) as per Annex-II.

rules.title: Risk-Based Approach for ML/FT
rules.description: NBFCs should take steps to identify and assess their ML/FT risk for customers, countries, and geographical areas, as well as for products/services/transactions/delivery channels. They should have policies, controls, and procedures in place to effectively manage and mitigate their risk adopting a risk-based approach.
rules.source_clause: Accordingly, NBFCs should take steps to identify and assess their ML/FT risk for customers, countries and geographical areas as also for products/ services/ transactions/delivery channels, in addition to what has been prescribed in our Master Circular dated July 1, 2011

rules.title: Enhanced Measures for High-Risk Customers
rules.description: NBFCs should adopt enhanced measures for products, services, and customers with a medium or high risk rating.
rules.source_clause: As a corollary, NBFCs would be required to adopt enhanced measures for products, services and customers with a medium or high risk rating.

rules.title: Reporting Format for Suspicious Transactions
rules.description: NBFCs should report information/data relating to Cash and Suspicious Transactions to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) in the prescribed format.
rules.source_clause: The present multiple data files reporting format mentioned in Annex-II and Annex-IV of para 28 c of the Master circular No 291 is being replaced by a new single XML file format

rules.title: Submission of Reports in Test Mode
rules.description: NBFCs should initiate submission of reports on the FINnet Gateway in ‘TEST MODE’ from August 31, 2012 to test their ability to upload the report electronically.
rules.source_clause: FIU-IND had  advised vide their letter F.No.9-29/2011-FIU-IND dated August 28, 2012, that all NBFCs should initiate submission of reports on the FINnet Gateway in ‘TEST MODE’ from August 31, 2012 to test their ability to upload the report electronically.

rules.title: Monitoring of Accounts with Terrorist Links
rules.description: NBFCs should develop a suitable mechanism through an appropriate policy framework for enhanced monitoring of accounts suspected of having terrorist links and swift identification of transactions.
rules.source_clause: In terms of PMLA Rules, suspicious transaction should include inter alia transactions which give rise to a reasonable ground of suspicion that these may involve financing of the activities relating to terrorism.

rules.title: Update of Consolidated List of Individuals/Entities
rules.description: NBFCs should ensure that the consolidated list of individuals and entities as circulated by Reserve Bank is updated.
rules.source_clause: As and when list of individuals and entities, approved by Security Council Committee established pursuant to various United Nations' Security Council Resolutions (UNSCRs), are received from Government of India, Reserve Bank circulates these to all banks and financial institutions (including NBFCs).

rules.title: Consideration of FATF Statements
rules.description: NBFCs should consider the information contained in the statements issued by FATF.
rules.source_clause: Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has issued  several Statements on risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of   various countries for example

rules.title: Ongoing Monitoring of High-Risk Accounts
rules.description: NBFCs should examine the background and purpose of transactions with persons from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements and countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations.
rules.source_clause: In terms of paragraph 4 of Annex-VI of the Master Circular No 184 dated July 1, 2010, ongoing monitoring is an essential element of effective KYC procedures.

rules.title: Prevention of Money Laundering
rules.description: NBFCs should strictly adhere to the guidelines on KYC/AML/CFT issued from time to time.
rules.source_clause: NBFCS were advised to strictly adhere to the guidelines on KYC/AML/CFT issued from time to time and to those relating to periodical updation of customer identification data after the account is opened and also to monitoring of transactions

rules.title: Suspicious Activities/Transactions
rules.description: NBFCs should monitor certain activities/transactions such as large cash transactions, multiple accounts under the same name, etc.
rules.source_clause: Some examples of suspicious activities/transactions to be monitored by the operating staff- Large Cash Transactions, Multiple accounts under the same name

rules.title: Risk Categorization of Customers
rules.description: Parameters of risk perception are clearly defined in terms of the nature of business activity, location of customer and his clients, mode of payments, volume of turnover, social and financial status etc.
rules.source_clause: (ii) Parameters of risk perception are clearly defined in terms of the nature of business activity, location of customer and his clients, mode of payments, volume of turnover, social and financial status etc.

rules.title: Documentation Requirements
rules.description: Documentation requirements and other information to be collected in respect of different categories of customers depending on perceived risk and keeping in mind the requirements of PML Act, 2002 and guidelines issued by Reserve Bank from time to time;
rules.source_clause: (iii) Documentation requirements and other information to be collected  in respect of  different categories of customers depending on perceived risk and keeping in mind  the requirements  of PML Act, 2002 and guidelines issued by Reserve Bank from time to time;

rules.title: Account Opening and Closure
rules.description: Not to open an account or close an existing account where the bank is unable to apply appropriate customer due diligence measures i.e. bank is unable to verify the identity and /or obtain documents required as per the risk categorisation due to non cooperation of the customer or non reliability of the data/information furnished to the bank.
rules.source_clause: Not to open an account or close an existing account where the bank is unable to apply appropriate customer due diligence measures i.e. bank is unable to verify the identity and /or obtain documents required as per the risk categorisation due to non cooperation of the customer or non reliability of the data/information furnished to the bank.

rules.title: Customer Due Diligence
rules.description: Necessary checks before opening a new account so as to ensure that the identity of the customer does not match with any person with known criminal background or with banned entities such as individual terrorists or terrorist organizations etc.
rules.source_clause: (vi) Necessary checks before opening a new account so as to ensure  that the identity of  the customer does not match with any person with known criminal  background or with banned entities such as individual terrorists or terrorist organizations etc.

rules.title: Low Risk Customer Categorization
rules.description: For the purpose of risk categorisation, individuals (other than High Net Worth) and entities whose identities and sources of wealth can be easily identified and transactions in whose accounts by and large conform to the known profile, may be categorised as low risk.
rules.source_clause: For the purpose of risk categorisation, individuals ( other than High Net Worth) and entities whose identities and sources of wealth can be easily identified and transactions in whose accounts by and large conform to the known profile, may be categorised as low risk.

rules.title: Medium and High Risk Customer Categorization
rules.description: Customers that are likely to pose a higher than average risk to the bank may be categorized as medium or high risk depending on customer's background, nature and location of activity, country of origin, sources of funds and his client profile etc.
rules.source_clause: Customers that are likely to pose a higher than average risk to the bank may be categorized as medium or high risk depending on  customer's background, nature  and location of activity, country of origin,  sources of funds and his client profile etc.

rules.title: Customer Identification Procedure
rules.description: The policy approved by the Board of banks should clearly spell out the Customer Identification Procedure to be carried out at different stages i.e. while establishing a banking relationship; carrying out a financial transaction or when the bank has a doubt about the authenticity/veracity or the adequacy of the previously obtained customer identification data.
rules.source_clause: The policy approved by the Board of banks should clearly spell out the Customer Identification Procedure to be carried out at different stages i.e. while establishing a banking relationship; carrying out a financial transaction or when the bank has a doubt about the authenticity/veracity or the adequacy of the previously obtained customer identification data.

rules.title: Beneficial Ownership Identification
rules.description: Banks need to identify the beneficial owner(s) and verify his/her/their identity in a manner so that it is satisfied that it knows who the beneficial owner(s) is/are.
rules.source_clause: If the bank decides to accept such accounts in terms of the Customer Acceptance Policy, the bank should take reasonable measures to identify the beneficial owner(s) and verify his/her/their identity in a manner so that it is satisfied that it knows who the beneficial owner(s) is/are.

rules.title: Beneficial Ownership Determination Procedure
rules.description: The procedure for determination of Beneficial Ownership is specified by the Government of India and banks need to follow the same.
rules.source_clause: The procedure as advised by the Government of India is as under: A. Where the client is a person other than an individual or trust, the banking company and financial institution, as the case may be, shall identify the beneficial owners of the client and take reasonable measures to verify the identity of such persons, through the following information:

rules.title: Transaction Threshold Limits
rules.description: Banks may prescribe threshold limits for a particular category of accounts and pay particular attention to transactions that exceed these limits.
rules.source_clause: The bank may prescribe   threshold limits for a particular category of accounts and pay particular attention to the transactions which exceed these limits.

rules.title: Monitoring of Cash Transactions
rules.description: Banks should ensure that its branches maintain proper records of all cash transactions (deposits and withdrawals) of Rs.10 lakh and above.
rules.source_clause: Banks should ensure that its branches continue to maintain proper record of all cash transactions ( deposits and withdrawals) of Rs.10 lakh and above.

rules.title: Internal Audit and Compliance
rules.description: Banks' internal audit and compliance functions have an important role in evaluating and ensuring adherence to the KYC policies and procedures.
rules.source_clause: Banks’ internal audit and compliance functions have an important role in evaluating and ensuring adherence to the KYC policies and procedures.

rules.title: Employee Training Programme
rules.description: Banks must have an ongoing employee training programme so that the members of the staff are adequately trained in KYC procedures.
rules.source_clause: Banks must have an ongoing employee training programme so that the members of the staff are adequately trained in KYC procedures.

rules.title: New Technologies and Money Laundering Threats
rules.description: Banks should pay special attention to any money laundering threats that may arise from new or developing technologies, including internet banking.
rules.source_clause: Banks should pay special attention to any money laundering threats that may arise from new or developing technologies including internet banking that might favour anonymity, and take measures, if needed, to prevent their use in money laundering schemes.

rules.title: KYC for Electronic Cards
rules.description: Banks should ensure that appropriate KYC procedures are duly applied before issuing cards to customers.
rules.source_clause: Banks should ensure that appropriate KYC procedures are duly applied before issuing the cards to the customers.

rules.title: KYC for Existing Accounts
rules.description: Banks should apply KYC norms to existing customers on the basis of materiality and risk.
rules.source_clause: While the revised guidelines will apply to all new customers, banks should apply the same to the existing customers on the basis of materiality and risk.

rules.title: Applicability to Branches and Subsidiaries Outside India
rules.description: The above guidelines shall also apply to the branches and majority owned subsidiaries located abroad, especially, in countries which do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations.
rules.source_clause: The above guidelines shall also apply to the branches and majority owned subsidiaries located abroad, especially, in countries which do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations, to the extent local laws permit.

rules.title: Appointment of Principal Officer
rules.description: Banks may appoint a senior management officer to be designated as Principal Officer, responsible for monitoring and reporting of all transactions.
rules.source_clause: Banks may appoint a senior management officer to be designated as Principal Officer. Principal Officer shall be located at the head/corporate office of the bank and shall be responsible for monitoring and reporting of all transactions and sharing of information as required under the law.

rules.title: Accounts of Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs)
rules.description: Banks should gather sufficient information on any person/customer of this category intending to establish a relationship and check all the information available on the person in the public domain.
rules.source_clause: Banks should gather sufficient information on any person/customer of this category intending to establish a relationship  and check all the information available on the person in the public domain.

rules.title: Accounts of Non-Face-to-Face Customers
rules.description: In the case of non-face-to-face customers, apart from applying the usual customer identification procedures, there must be specific and adequate procedures to mitigate the higher risk involved.
rules.source_clause: In the case of non-face-to-face customers, apart from applying the usual customer identification procedures, there must be specific and adequate procedures to mitigate the higher risk involved.

rules.title: Third Party Certification Requirements
rules.description: In cases where the bank relies on third-party certification/introduction, the third party must be a regulated and supervised entity with adequate KYC systems in place.
rules.source_clause: In such cases, it must be ensured that the third party is a regulated and supervised entity and has adequate KYC systems in place.

rules.title: Correspondent Banking Due Diligence
rules.description: Banks should gather sufficient information to understand fully the nature of the business of the correspondent/respondent bank, including management, major business activities, level of AML/CFT compliance, and regulatory/supervisory framework.
rules.source_clause: Banks should gather sufficient information to understand fully the nature of the business of the correspondent/respondent bank. Information on the other bank’s management, major business activities, level of AML/CFT compliance, purpose of opening the account, identity of any third party entities that will use the correspondent banking services, and regulatory/supervisory framework in the correspondent's/respondent’s country may be of special relevance.

rules.title: Approval of Correspondent Banking Relationships
rules.description: Correspondent banking relationships should be established only with the approval of the Board, and proposals approved by a delegated committee should be put up to the Board for post facto approval.
rules.source_clause: While it is desirable that such relationships should be established only with the approval of the  Board, in case the Boards of some banks wish to delegate the power to an administrative authority, they may delegate the power to a committee headed by the Chairman/CEO of the bank while laying down clear parameters for approving such relationships. Proposals approved by the Committee should invariably be put up  to the Board at its next meeting for post facto approval.

rules.title: Documentation of Correspondent Banking Relationships
rules.description: The responsibilities of each bank with whom a correspondent banking relationship is established should be clearly documented.
rules.source_clause: The responsibilities of each bank with whom correspondent banking relationship is established should be clearly documented.

rules.title: Payable-Through-Accounts Requirements
rules.description: In the case of payable-through-accounts, the correspondent bank should be satisfied that the respondent bank has verified the identity of the customers having direct access to the accounts and is undertaking ongoing 'due diligence' on them.
rules.source_clause: In the case of payable-through-accounts, the correspondent bank should be satisfied that the respondent bank has verified the identity of the customers having direct access to the accounts and is undertaking ongoing 'due diligence' on them.

rules.title: Shell Bank Prohibition
rules.description: Banks should refuse to enter into a correspondent relationship with a 'shell bank' (a bank which is incorporated in a country where it has no physical presence and is unaffiliated to any regulated financial group).
rules.source_clause: Banks should refuse to enter into a correspondent relationship with a “shell bank” (i.e. a bank which is incorporated in a country where it has no physical presence and

rules.title: AML Policies and Procedures for Respondent Banks
rules.description: Banks should ensure that their respondent banks have anti-money laundering policies and procedures in place and apply enhanced 'due diligence' procedures for transactions carried out through the correspondent accounts.
rules.source_clause: Banks should ensure that their respondent banks have anti money laundering policies and procedures in place and apply enhanced 'due diligence' procedures for transactions carried out through the correspondent accounts.

rules.title: KYC Requirements for Partnership Firms
rules.description: For partnership firms, banks should obtain the legal name, address, names of all partners and their addresses, telephone numbers of the firm and partners, registration certificate (if registered), partnership deed, and power of attorney granted to a partner or employee.
rules.source_clause: Accounts of partnership firms - Legal name - Address - Names of all partners and their addresses - Telephone numbers of the firm and partners (i) Registration certificate, if registered  (ii) Partnership deed (iii) Power of Attorney granted to a partner or an employee of the firm to transact business on its behalf

rules.title: KYC Requirements for Trusts and Foundations
rules.description: For trusts and foundations, banks should obtain the names of trustees, settlers, beneficiaries and signatories, names and addresses of the founder, managers/directors and beneficiaries, and telephone/fax numbers.
rules.source_clause: Accounts of trusts & foundations - Names of trustees, settlers, beneficiaries and signatories - Names and addresses of the founder, the managers/directors and the beneficiaries - Telephone/fax numbers

rules.title: KYC Requirements for Proprietary Concerns
rules.description: For proprietary concerns, banks should obtain proof of the name, address and activity of the concern, such as registration certificate, certificate/licence issued by the Municipal authorities under Shop & Establishment Act, sales and income tax returns, CST/VAT certificate, or certificate/registration document issued by Sales Tax/Service Tax/Professional Tax authorities.
rules.source_clause: i)   Proof of the name, address and activity of the concern, like registration certificate (in the case of a registered concern), certificate/licence issued by the Municipal authorities under Shop & Establishment Act, sales and income tax returns, CST / VAT certificate, certificate / registration document issued by Sales Tax / Service Tax / Professional Tax authorities, Licence issued by the Registering authority like

rules.title: Customer Service and Identifiable Contact
rules.description: All deposit receipts must bear the name and Registered Office address of the NBFC and indicate the name of the persons authorised by the NBFC and their addresses who mobilised the deposit and the link office with the telephone number.
rules.source_clause: All deposit receipts should bear the name and Registered Office address of the NBFC and must invariably indicate the name of the persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc. and their addresses who mobilised the deposit and the link office with the telephone number of such officer and/or persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc.

rules.title: Senior Management Approval for PEP Customers
rules.description: NBFCs are advised to obtain senior management approval to continue the business relationship and subject the account to CDD measures as applicable to customers of PEP category, including enhanced monitoring on an ongoing basis.
rules.review_note: The source_clause '14. A' was not found verbatim in the page text. The correct source_clause seems to be '14.' as the page text mentions '14. Accounts of proprietary concerns' but not 'A'. The rule's source_clause might need to be updated for accuracy.

rules.title: Ongoing Monitoring of Transactions
rules.description: Banks should effectively monitor and control transactions to reduce risk, understanding normal and reasonable customer activity, and identifying transactions that fall outside the regular pattern of activity.
rules.source_clause: Ongoing monitoring is an essential element of effective KYC procedures.  Banks can effectively control and reduce their risk only if they have an understanding of the normal and reasonable activity of the customer so that they have the means of identifying transactions that fall outside the regular pattern of activity.
rules.review_note: The numeric threshold mentioned in the page text is Rs.10 lakh, which is not present in the rule. The rule does not specify any threshold, but the page text does.

rules.title: KYC Programme Implementation
rules.description: The Board of Directors of the bank should ensure that an effective KYC programme is put in place by establishing appropriate procedures and ensuring their effective implementation.
rules.source_clause: The Board of Directors of the bank should ensure that an effective KYC programme is put in place by establishing appropriate procedures and ensuring their effective implementation.

rules.title: Screening Mechanism for Recruitment
rules.description: NBFCs should put in place an adequate screening mechanism as an integral part of their recruitment/hiring process of personnel.
rules.source_clause: It would, therefore, be necessary that adequate screening mechanism is put in place by NBFCs as an integral part of their recruitment/hiring process of personnel.

rules.title: KYC/AML/CFT Awareness among Staff
rules.description: NBFCs may consider the indicative list of suspicious activities contained in Annex-V of the CC No.126 dated August 05, 2008.
rules.source_clause: In the context of creating KYC/AML awareness among the staff and for generating alerts for suspicious transactions, NBFCs may consider the indicative list of suspicious activities contained in Annex-V of the CC No.126 dated August 05, 2008.

rules.title: Customer Education
rules.description: Banks should prepare specific literature/pamphlets to educate the customer of the objectives of the KYC programme.
rules.source_clause: There is, therefore, a need for banks to prepare specific literature/ pamphlets etc. so as to educate the customer of the objectives of the KYC programme.
